root_cause.text: The fsl-cpm SPI driver’s `fsl_spi_prepare_message()` could switch 8-bit transfers to 16-bit mode based only on transfer length threshold and `SPI_CPM1`, without verifying that `t->len` was even, causing 16-bit handling of odd-sized buffers and a buffer overrun.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the missing parity check `!(t->len & 1)` to the condition that changes `t->bits_per_word` from 8 to 16, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that commit `fc96ec826bce` “failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode,” which led to “a buffer overrun in the fsl-cpm driver when that size is odd.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds the missing parity check `!(t->len & 1)` to the condition that changes `t->bits_per_word` from 8 to 16, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that commit `fc96ec826bce` “failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode,” which led to “a buffer overrun in the fsl-cpm driver when that size is odd.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Only switch large SPI_CPM1 transfers to 16-bit mode when the transfer length is even to avoid mishandling odd-length transfers.
intent_record.what: In fsl_spi_prepare_message(), the condition that changes t->bits_per_word from 8 to 16 for large transfers on SPI_CPM1 was extended by adding a new requirement: !(t->len & 1), meaning the transfer length must be even.
intent_record.how: At runtime, 8-bit transfers of length 256 or more on SPI_CPM1 will now only be promoted to 16-bit mode when the transfer length is evenly divisible by 2. This prevents odd-length transfers from being handled as 16-bit words, avoiding incorrect word packing or incomplete final-byte handling.

grouping_result.intent: Only switch large SPI_CPM1 transfers to 16-bit mode when the transfer length is even to avoid mishandling odd-length transfers.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an even-length check before switching SPI_CPM1 transfers to 16-bit mode, preventing odd-sized buffers from being handled as 16-bit and overrunning.

candidates.rationale: This conditional decides to switch an 8-bit transfer into 16-bit mode based on length threshold alone, without checking that t->len is even. That missing validation is the direct root cause enabling odd-length buffers to be handled as 16-bit transfers.
This statement performs the unsafe mode switch to 16-bit transfers after the incomplete condition, causing odd-sized buffers to be processed with 16-bit semantics and potentially overrun.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root cause because it decides whether to convert an 8-bit transfer into 16-bit mode using only the size threshold and SPI_CPM1 path, without validating that t->len is even. That omission allows odd-length buffers to be treated as 16-bit transfers.
This statement performs the unsafe mode switch to 16-bit transfers after the incomplete condition, causing odd-sized buffers to be processed with 16-bit semantics and enabling the buffer overrun.
